resources.string: Right atrium cutaway
Right atrium · Opened and spread, front wall at image left
Upper caval opening
The superior vena cava enters from above, returning blood from the head, neck, upper limbs, and chest to the smooth back of the atrium.
Pectinate muscles
These comb-like ridges fan across the front wall and right atrial appendage. The raised terminal crest separates them from the smooth region that receives the venae cavae.
Fossa ovalis
This shallow oval depression lies in the wall between the atria. It marks the former site of the fetal opening between the two chambers.
Lower caval opening
The inferior vena cava enters from below, returning blood from the abdomen, pelvis, and lower limbs. The smaller coronary sinus opening lies just above and toward the septum.
Left atrium cutaway
Left atrium · Opened from the front, body left at image right
Right pulmonary veins
The two openings on this side usually receive oxygen-rich blood from the right lung. The upper opening is for the superior vein and the lower opening is for the inferior vein.
Left pulmonary veins
The superior and inferior veins from the left lung usually enter through separate openings behind the left atrial appendage.
Atrial appendage
The left atrial appendage is a narrow muscular pouch. Its inner surface has comb-like pectinate ridges that stay within the pouch.
Smooth back wall
The back wall around the four pulmonary vein openings is smooth. Blood entering here passes through the atrium and down through the mitral valve to the left ventricle.
Right ventricle cutaway
Right ventricle · Opened from the front, inlet at image left
Outflow tract
The smooth muscular outflow tract, or infundibulum, narrows upward to the pulmonary valve. Blood passes through that valve into the pulmonary trunk.
Moderator band
This muscular bridge crosses from the wall between the ventricles to the base of the anterior papillary muscle on the free-wall side.
Trabeculae carneae
Coarse muscle ridges line the lower part of the chamber. They give its inner surface a rough texture unlike the smooth upper outflow tract.
Left ventricle cutaway
Left ventricle · Oblique long-axis cutaway, apex at lower right
Thick muscle wall
The muscular wall is thicker than in the right ventricle. It surrounds the long chamber, which tapers toward the apex of the heart.
Tendinous cords
These fine cords join the mitral leaflets to the papillary muscles. They help hold the leaflets in place when the ventricle contracts. The aortic valve has no such cords.
Papillary muscles
Two groups of papillary muscles project from the ventricular wall. Their tips anchor the cords attached to both mitral leaflets.
